H.AMDT.595 Amendment (A001) offered by Mr. Oberstar. (consideration: CR H2602-2603; text: CR H2603)Amendment ensures that program evaluations assess whether the implementation of a comprehensive conservation and management plan is achieving its stated goals; (2) enhances public education on the connections between air land and water and the potential impacts on estuarine health; (3) strikes the existing statutory priority list for estuaries to clarify that existing and proposed management conferences enter or remain in the program on a competitive basis and (4) removes individuals from the list of approved recipients for grants under this program.
DEBATE - Pursuant to the provisions of H.Res. 1248 the Committee of the Whole proceeded with 10 minutes of debate on the Oberstar amendment.
H.AMDT.595 On agreeing to the Oberstar amendment (A001) Agreed to by voice vote.

H.AMDT.596 Amendment (A002) offered by Mr. Oberstar. (consideration: CR H2603-2605; text: CR H2603-2604)Amendment requires the administrator to evaluate the effectiveness of the program; identifies and disseminates best practices for positive outcomes; and identifies and limits redundant rules regulations and reporting requirements.
DEBATE - Pursuant to the provisions of H.Res. 1248 the Committee of the Whole proceeded with 10 minutes of debate on the Oberstar amendment.
H.AMDT.596 On agreeing to the Oberstar amendment (A002) Agreed to by voice vote.

H.AMDT.597 Amendment (A003) offered by Mr. Kagen. (consideration: CR H2605; text: CR H2605)Amendment requires estuary programs to include in their comprehensive conservation and management plans a coordinated monitoring strategy between federal state and local entities.
DEBATE - Pursuant to the provisions of H.Res. 1248 the Committee of the Whole proceeded with 10 minutes of debate on the Kagen amendment.
H.AMDT.597 On agreeing to the Kagen amendment (A003) Agreed to by voice vote.

H.AMDT.598 Amendment (A004) offered by Mr. Schauer. (consideration: CR H2605-2607; text: CR H2605)Amendment defines "estuary" under the Clean Water Act to include Great Lakes waters and wetlands that are similar to traditional estuaries covered by the National Estuary Program.
DEBATE - Pursuant to the provisions of H.Res. 1248 the Committee of the Whole proceeded with 10 minutes of debate on the Schauer amendment.
H.AMDT.598 On agreeing to the Schauer amendment (A004) Agreed to by voice vote.

H.AMDT.599 Amendment (A005) offered by Ms. Moore (WI). (consideration: CR H2607; text: CR H2607)Amendment adds trend monitoring of the introduction and establishment of nonnative species including their pathways for introduction in estuarine zones to the list of research programs the Administrator can carry out.
DEBATE - Pursuant to the provisions of H.Res. 1248 the Committee of the Whole proceeded with 10 minutes of debate on the Moore (WI) amendment.
H.AMDT.599 On agreeing to the Moore (WI) amendment (A005) Agreed to by voice vote.

H.AMDT.600 Amendment (A006) offered by Ms. Shea-Porter. (consideration: CR H2607-2608 H2610-2611; text: CR H2607)Amendment ensures that comprehensive conservation and management plans address the impacts and potential effects of sea level change.
DEBATE - Pursuant to the provisions of H.Res. 1248 the Committee of the Whole proceeded with 10 minutes of debate on the Shea-Porter amendment.

POSTPONED PROCEEDINGS - At the conclusion of debate on the Shea-Porter amendment the Chair put the question on adoption of the amendment and by voice vote announced that the ayes had prevailed. Ms. Shea-Porter demanded a recorded vote and the Chair postponed further proceedings on the question of adoption of the amendment until later in the legislative day.

H.AMDT.601 Amendment (A007) offered by Mr. Kratovil. (consideration: CR H2608-2609; text: CR H2608)Amendment makes explicit that collaborative processes should be used to develop the management plan by calling for the equitable inclusion of all relevant estuary stakeholders; the use of neutral facilitators and processes to resolve conflicts; and the inclusion and use of up-to-date information among other considerations.
DEBATE - Pursuant to the provisions of H.Res. 1248 the Committee of the Whole proceeded with 10 minutes of debate on the Kratovil amendment.
H.AMDT.601 On agreeing to the Kratovil amendment (A007) Agreed to by voice vote.

H.AMDT.775 Amendment (A001) offered by Mr. Holden. (consideration: CR H6785-6786 H6788; text: CR H6785)Amendment clarifies that loan funds under the bill may not be used to purchase manufactured homes; makes technical corrections to a Comptroller General report; prohibits provision of funds to certain contractors and makes certain Federal Employees ineligible for loans. House resolved itself into the Committee of the Whole House on the state of the Union pursuant to H. Res. 1300 and Rule XVIII.

GENERAL DEBATE - The Committee of the Whole proceeded with one hour of general debate on H.R. 5013.

H.AMDT.602 Amendment (A001) offered by Mr. Skelton. (consideration: CR H2968-2969; text: CR H2968)Amendment makes various technical corrections to the bill and also provides that nothing in contracts for military purpose non-developmental items shall restrict or otherwise affect the rights in technical data of the Government the contractor or any subcontractor for items developed by the contractor or subcontractor exclusively at private expense.
DEBATE - Pursuant to the provisions of H.Res. 1300 the Committee of the Whole proceeded with 10 minutes of debate on the Skelton amendment.
H.AMDT.602 On agreeing to the Skelton amendment (A001) Agreed to by voice vote.

H.AMDT.603 Amendment (A002) offered by Mr. Sessions. (consideration: CR H2969-2970; text: CR H2969)An amendment numbered 2 printed in House Report 111-467 to provide that nothing in the Act or amendments made by it shall be construed to affect the competition requirements of 10 U.S.C. 2304 (contract competition requirements).
DEBATE - Pursuant to the provisions of H.Res. 1300 the Committee of the Whole proceeded with 10 minutes of debate on the Sessions amendment.
H.AMDT.603 On agreeing to the Sessions amendment (A002) Agreed to by voice vote.

H.AMDT.604 Amendment (A003) offered by Mr. Andrews. (consideration: CR H2970; text: CR H2970)Amendment supports a diverse workforce development program with respect to career development for civilian and military personnel in the acquisition workforce.
DEBATE - Pursuant to the provisions of H.Res. 1300 the Committee of the Whole proceeded with 10 minutes of debate on the Andrews amendment.
H.AMDT.604 On agreeing to the Andrews amendment (A003) Agreed to by voice vote.

H.AMDT.605 Amendment (A004) offered by Mr. Hall (NY). (consideration: CR H2970-2971 H2982-2983; text: CR H2970)Amendment requires the Director of the Office of Performance Assessment and Root Cause Analysis ("PARCA") to include performance assessments with significant findings in its annual report as well as submission of egregious problems (as defined by the PARCA Director) to the Armed Services Committees.
DEBATE - Pursuant to the provisions of H.Res. 1300 the Committee of the Whole proceeded with 10 minutes of debate on the Hall (NY) amendment.

POSTPONED PROCEEDINGS - At the conclusion of debate on the Hall (NY) amendment the Chair put the question on adoption of the amendment and by voice vote announced that the ayes had prevailed. Mr. Hall (NY) demanded a recorded vote and the Chair postponed further proceedings on the question of adoption of the amendment until later in the legislative day.

H.AMDT.606 Amendment (A005) offered by Ms. Edwards (MD). (consideration: CR H2971-2972; text: CR H2971)Amendment directs the DOD to engage in outreach to businesses in the vicinity of DOD installations to notify them of opportunities to obtain contracts and subcontracts to perform work at such installations.
DEBATE - Pursuant to the provisions of H.Res. 1300 the Committee of the Whole proceeded with 10 minutes of debate on the Edewards (MD) amendment.
H.AMDT.606 On agreeing to the Edwards (MD) amendment (A005) Agreed to by voice vote.

H.AMDT.607 Amendment (A006) offered by Ms. Moore (WI). (consideration: CR H2972-2973; text: CR H2972)Amendment specifies that assessment metrics required to measure contractor performance include "compliance of such contractors with department policy regarding the use of certain small businesses".
DEBATE - Pursuant to the provisions of H.Res. 1300 the Committee of the Whole proceeded with 10 minutes of debate on the Moore (WI) amendment.
H.AMDT.607 On agreeing to the Moore (WI) amendment (A006) Agreed to by voice vote.

H.AMDT.608 Amendment (A007) offered by Mr. Murphy (CT). (consideration: CR H2973-2974; text: CR H2973)Amendment specifies that Title IV assistance in the legislation (Expansion of the Industrial Base) be limited to firms within the national technology and industrial base which is defined in section 2500(1) of title 10 United States Code as those companies in the United States and Canada.
DEBATE - Pursuant to the provisions of H.Res. 1300 the Committee of the Whole proceeded with 10 minutes of debate on the Murphy (CT) amendment.
H.AMDT.608 On agreeing to the Murphy (CT) amendment (A007) Agreed to by voice vote.

H.AMDT.609 Amendment (A008) offered by Mr. Quigley. (consideration: CR H2974; text: CR H2974)Amendment includes energy efficiency as one of the metrics that may be used in performance assessment of defense acquisitions and would include energy efficiency of weapons systems as one of the items considered in the Secretary's review of defense acquisition guidance.
DEBATE - Pursuant to the provisions of H.Res. 1300 the Committee of the Whole proceeded with 10 minutes of debate on the Quigley amendment number 8.
H.AMDT.609 On agreeing to the Quigley amendment (A008) Agreed to by voice vote.

H.AMDT.610 Amendment (A009) offered by Mr. Quigley. (consideration: CR H2974-2975; text: CR H2974)Amendment directs the Cost Assessment and Program Evaluation (CAPE) in its next report to Congress to (1) assess whether and to what extent program cost estimators for major defense acquisition programs are independent and (2) whether a lack of independence affects their ability to generate reliable cost estimates.
DEBATE - Pursuant to the provisions of H.Res. 1300 the Committee of the Whole proceeded with 10 minutes of debate on the Quigley amendment number 9.
H.AMDT.610 On agreeing to the Quigley amendment (A009) Agreed to by voice vote.

H.AMDT.611 Amendment (A010) offered by Mr. Schrader. (consideration: CR H2975-2976; text: CR H2975)Amendment prohibits the award of contracts for personal services by any DOD component for the purpose of obtaining the services of a senior mentor. Nothing would prohibit DOD from hiring retired generals and flag officers as "senior mentors" under the highly qualified expert provision of 5 U.S.C. section 9903 with additional financial disclosure and conflict of interest requirements in place.
DEBATE - Pursuant to the provisions of H.Res. 1300 the Committee of the Whole proceeded with 10 minutes of debate on the Schrader amendment.
H.AMDT.611 On agreeing to the Schrader amendment (A010) Agreed to by voice vote.

H.AMDT.612 Amendment (A011) offered by Mr. Connolly (VA). (consideration: CR H2976-2977 H2983; text: CR H2976)Amendment creates an Industrial Base Council within the DOD supported by existing personnel and funds to provide recommendations to the Secretary on budget and policy matters related to the industrial base and requires an annual report to Congress on the Council's activities.
DEBATE - Pursuant to the provisions of H.Res. 1300 the Committee of the Whole proceeded with 10 minutes of debate on the Connolly (VA) amendment.

H.AMDT.718 Amendment (A001) offered by Ms. Waters. (consideration: CR H5641-5644; text: CR H5641-5643)Amendment phases out subsidized premiums for severe repetitive loss properties substantially damaged or improved properties and policy holders who voluntarily allow flood coverage to lapse; clarifies application of actuarial rate phase-in for pre-FIRM properties sold after enactment; provides preferred rate premium for properties participating in NFIP during newly established 5-year delay in mandatory flood insurance purchase requirement; expands availability of installment premium payment program to all policyholders; clarifies that the FEMA Director may work directly with property owners to make mitigation grants for certain repetitive loss properties where States or communities are either unable or unwilling to address repetitive loss issues with a property owner; allows commercial properties with swimming pools located below the base flood level to enclose those pools with breakaway walls outside of hu

(consideration: CR H5644-5645; text: CR H5644)Amendment requires FEMA to annually submit a report to Congress (no later than December 31 of each calendar year) on the effectiveness of grants awarded to local government agencies the activities conducted and the effect of such activities on the retention or acquisition of flood insurance coverage.
DEBATE - Pursuant to the provisions of H.Res. 1517 the Committee of the Whole proceeded with 10 minutes of debate on the Putnam amendment.

(consideration: CR H5645-5646; text: CR H5645)Amendment authorizes the FEMA administrator to reimburse property owners or entity or jurisdiction acting on their behalf for any expenses that they incurred in order to file for a letter of map amendment if they are ultimately successful in petitioning the exclusion of their property from a flood zone between fiscal year 2007 to the present as well as in the future.

Ms. Waters demanded a recorded vote and the Chair postponed further proceedings on the question of adoption of the amendment until later in the legislative day.

H.AMDT.722 Amendment (A005) offered by Mr. Taylor. (consideration: CR H5646-5648; text: CR H5646-5647)Amendment prohibits the Write Your Own insurance companies that contract with NFIP from excluding coverage of wind damage under their own policies solely because flooding also caused damage to the property and establishes requirements for adjustment by WYO insurers when there are claims on the same property from the same event for flood damage covered by NFIP and for wind damage covered by the WYO insurer.
DEBATE - Pursuant to the provisions of H.Res. 1517 the Committee of the Whole proceeded with 10 minutes of debate on the Taylor amendment.

H.AMDT.710 Amendment (A001) offered by Mr. Ackerman. (consideration: CR H4816-4817; text: CR H4816)Amendment requires covered organizations to report required disclosures to shareholders members or donors in a "clear and conspicuous manner.".
DEBATE - Pursuant to the provisions of H.Res. 1468 the Committee of the Whole proceeded with 10 minutes of debate on the Ackerman amendment.

POSTPONED PROCEEDINGS - At the conclusion of debate on the King (IA) amendment the Chair put the question on adoption of the amendment and by voice vote announced that the noes had prevailed. H.AMDT.712 Amendment (A003) offered by Mr. Kucinich. (consideration: CR H4818-4820; text: CR H4818)Amendment clarifies that the provisions of the bill would apply to companies with leases with the Federal Government allowing them to drill for oil and gas in the Outer Continental Shelf.
DEBATE - Pursuant to the provisions of H.Res. 1468 the Committee of the Whole proceeded with 10 minutes of debate on the Kucinich amendment.

H.AMDT.713 Amendment (A004) offered by Mr. Pascrell. (consideration: CR H4820-4822; text: CR H4820)Amendment prohibits political expenditures by corporations with significant foreign government ownership and corporations that have a majority of shares owned by foreign nationals.
DEBATE - Pursuant to the provisions of H.Res. 1468 the Committee of the Whole proceeded with 10 minutes of debate on the Pascrell amendment.
H.AMDT.713 On agreeing to the Pascrell amendment (A004) Agreed to by voice vote.

H.AMDT.714 Amendment (A005) offered by Mr. Murphy Patrick. (consideration: CR H4822-4824 H4824-4825; text: CR H4822-4823)Amendment requires that special interests outside a given district or state which are trying to impact an election in that district or state must use enhanced advertisement disclaimers to include the city and state of the ad funder's residence or principle office.
DEBATE - Pursuant to the provisions of H.Res. 1468 the Committee of the Whole proceeded with 10 minutes of debate on the Patrick Murphy amendment.

GENERAL DEBATE - The Committee of the Whole proceeded with one hour of general debate on H.R. 5297.

H.AMDT.694 Amendment (A001) offered by Mr. Israel. (consideration: CR H4529; text: CR H4529)Amendment adds veteran- and women- owned businesses to the groups that will receive outreach under the Small Business Lending Fund established by the bill; adds veteran-owned businesses to those businesses that should receive consideration in the Fund; adds veterans to the study on lending assistance; and requires the study to report not just on the number of loans made to women- veteran- and minority-owned businesses but the percent of loans that go to them as a part of the program.
DEBATE - Pursuant to the provisions of H.Res. 1436 the Committee of the Whole proceeded with 10 minutes of debate on the Israel amendment.

POSTPONED PROCEEDINGS - At the conclusion of debate on the Israel amendment the Chair put the question on adoption of the amendment and by voice vote announced that the ayes had prevailed. Mr. Israel demanded a recorded vote and the Chair postponed further proceedings on the question of adoption of the amendment until later in the legislative day.

H.AMDT.695 Amendment (A002) offered by Mr. Nye. (consideration: CR H4529-4531; text: CR H4529-4530)Amendment adds four stipulations to the Small Business Lending Fund to safeguard small businesses in the bill: 1) provides a definition of what constitutes a small business in order to ensure that funds are properly lent; 2) links lending incentives to volume in order to open up the credit markets to every qualified small business; 3) sets a hardened baseline when measuring a bank's lending record; and 4) includes small business lending companies with less than $10 billion in assets as qualified financial institutions alongside community banks and small credit unions.
DEBATE - Pursuant to the provisions of H.Res. 1436 the Committee of the Whole proceeded with 10 minutes of debate on the Nye amendment.
H.AMDT.695 On agreeing to the Nye amendment (A002) Agreed to by voice vote.
H.AMDT.696 Amendment (A003) offered by Mr. Minnick. (consideration: CR H4531; text: CR H4531)Amendment as modified makes nonowner-occupied commercial real estate loans eligible for the program.
DEBATE - Pursuant to the provisions of H.Res. 1436 the Committee of the Whole proceeded with 10 minutes of debate on the Minnick amendment.
H.AMDT.696 Minnick amendment (A003) modified by unanimous consent.
H.AMDT.696 On agreeing to the Minnick amendment (A003) as modified Agreed to by voice vote. (text as modified: CR H4531)

H.AMDT.697 Amendment (A004) offered by Mr. Perlmutter. (consideration: CR H4531-4533; text: CR H4531-4532)Amendment allows small banks to amortize losses or write-downs on commercial real estate loans over a 10-year period freeing up more capital for these small institutions to lend to small businesses.
DEBATE - Pursuant to the provisions of H.Res. 1436 the Committee of the Whole proceeded with 10 minutes of debate on the Perlmutter amendment.
H.AMDT.697 On agreeing to the Perlmutter amendment (A004) Agreed to by voice vote.

H.AMDT.698 Amendment (A005) offered by Mr. Price (GA). (consideration: CR H4533; text: CR H4533)An amendment numbered 6 printed in part C of House Report 111-506 to express the Sense of Congress that small business lending is being hindered by mixed messages from federal financial regulators.
DEBATE - Pursuant to the provisions of H.Res. 1436 the Committee of the Whole proceeded with 10 minutes of debate on the Price (GA) amendment.
H.AMDT.698 On agreeing to the Price (GA) amendment (A005) Agreed to by voice vote.
H.AMDT.699 Amendment (A006) offered by Mr. Green Al. (consideration: CR H4533-4535; text: CR H4534)Amendment improves disclosures by eligible institutions receiving funding under the program.
DEBATE - Pursuant to the provisions of H.Res. 1436 the Committee of the Whole proceeded with 10 minutes of debate on the Al Green (TX) amendment.
H.AMDT.699 On agreeing to the Green Al amendment (A006) Agreed to by voice vote.

H.AMDT.700 Amendment (A007) offered by Mr. Driehaus. (consideration: CR H4535-4536; text: CR H4535)Amendment establishes a new Office of Small Business Lending Fund Oversight under the authority of the Treasury Inspector General.
DEBATE - Pursuant to the provisions of H.Res. 1436 the Committee of the Whole proceeded with 10 minutes of debate on the Driehaus amendment.
H.AMDT.700 On agreeing to the Driehaus amendment (A007) Agreed to by voice vote.

H.AMDT.701 Amendment (A008) offered by Mr. Michaud. (consideration: CR H4536-4537; text: CR H4537)Amendment ensures that State-run venture capital fund programs will be eligible to participate in the program and clarifies that State financing programs will be eligible for the program as long as their use of new funds meets the business-sized requirements in the bill.
DEBATE - Pursuant to the provisions of H.Res. 1436 the Committee of the Whole proceeded with 10 minutes of debate on the Michaud amendment.
H.AMDT.701 On agreeing to the Michaud amendment (A008) Agreed to by voice vote.

H.AMDT.702 Amendment (A009) offered by Mr. Cao. (consideration: CR H4537-4538; text: CR H4537)Amendment provides funding to eligible institutions that serve small businesses in communities that have suffered negative economic effects as a result of the Deepwater Horizon oil spill with particular consideration to States along the coast of the Gulf of Mexico.
DEBATE - Pursuant to the provisions of H.Res. 1436 the Committee of the Whole proceeded with 10 minutes of debate on the Cao amendment.

POSTPONED PROCEEDINGS - At the conclusion of debate on the Cao amendment the Chair put the question on adoption of the amendment and by voice vote announced that the ayes had prevailed. Ms. Jackson Lee (TX) demanded a recorded vote and the Chair postponed further proceedings on the question of adoption of the amendment until later in the legislative day.

H.AMDT.703 Amendment (A010) offered by Ms. Sanchez Loretta. (consideration: CR H4538-4539; text: CR H4538)Amendment provides that as part of the selection criteria the small business administrator would examine the extent to which the investment company would concentrate its investment capital on targeted industries.
DEBATE - Pursuant to the provisions of H.Res. 1436 the Committee of the Whole proceeded with 10 minutes of debate on the Loretta Sanchez(CA) amendment.
H.AMDT.703 On agreeing to the Sanchez Loretta amendment (A010) Agreed to by voice vote.

H.AMDT.704 Amendment (A011) offered by Mr. Cuellar. (consideration: CR H4539; text: CR H4539)Amendment requires the Secretary to take into consideration areas with high unemployment rates that exceed the national average to increase opportunities for small business development.
DEBATE - Pursuant to the provisions of H.Res. 1436 the Committee of the Whole proceeded with 10 minutes of debate on the Cuellar amendment.
H.AMDT.704 On agreeing to the Cuellar amendment (A011) Agreed to by voice vote.

H.AMDT.705 Amendment (A012) offered by Mr. Braley (IA). (consideration: CR H4539-4540; text: CR H4539-4540)Amendment requires the use of plain writing by the Department of the Treasury and the Small Business Administration for documents relevant to obtaining a benefit or service under the bill.
DEBATE - Pursuant to the provisions of H.Res. 1436 the Committee of the Whole proceeded with 10 minutes of debate on the Braley amendment.
H.AMDT.705 On agreeing to the Braley (IA) amendment (A012) Agreed to by voice vote.

H.AMDT.706 Amendment (A013) offered by Mr. Loebsack. (consideration: CR H4540-4541; text: CR H4540)Amendment includes a Sense of Congress stating that agriculture operations farms and rural communities should receive equal consideration through lending activities for small businesses particularly small and mid-size farms and agriculture operations and further states that attention should be given to ensuring there is adequate small business credit and financing availability in the agriculture and farming sectors.
DEBATE - Pursuant to the provisions of H.Res. 1436 the Committee of the Whole proceeded with 10 minutes of debate on the Loebsack amendment.
H.AMDT.706 On agreeing to the Loebsack amendment (A013) Agreed to by voice vote.

H.AMDT.707 Amendment (A014) offered by Mr. Green Al. (consideration: CR H4541-4542; text: CR H4541)Amendment requires the inclusion of linguistically and culturally appropriate outreach to the applicant's small business lending plan; provides for linguistically and culturally appropriate minority outreach and advertising; explicitly states minority-owned financial institutions are eligible for consideration of by the Secretary for funding; and requires the Secretary to the extent possible to disaggregate the results of the report on women-owned and minority-owned business by ethnic group and gender.
DEBATE - Pursuant to the provisions of H.Res. 1436 the Committee of the Whole proceeded with 10 minutes of debate on the Al Green (TX) amendment.

H.AMDT.320 Amendment (A001) offered by Mr. Pastor (AZ). (consideration: CR H8133-8134 H8143-8144; text: CR H8133)Manager's amendment provides $2.5 million for the Northern Border Regional Commission to address economic challenges in border counties from Maine to New York; $1.8 million for the Corps of Engineers to help address the backlog of regulatory permit applications; and $45 million for energy efficiency and renewable energy. The amendment also prohibits use of funds in the bill to purchase lightbulbs unless they are "Energy Star" qualified or have the "Federal Energy Management Program" designation and prohibits use of funds for purchase of passenger motor vehicles other than those manufactured by Ford General Motors or Chrysler. Finally the amendment decreases funding for Corps of Engineers' programs and expenses by $10.8 million; the Department of Energy departmental administration by $30 million; the office of electricity by $15 million and other defense activities by $2.5 million.
